entries.clue: Sinister reputation's surpassed (4,8)

blocks.note: sinister is Latin for left, and heraldry still uses it that way
standing = reputation, as in 'a person of some standing'

annotation.surface: Someone's dark reputation has been outdone by an even darker one.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sinister' reads as evil, but here it is just the left-hand side. To leave someone standing is to outpace them easily.
annotation.definitionFit: If you leave a rival standing, you have surpassed them by a wide margin.

entries.clue: Brief result of amateur boxing scam (7)

indicatorNotes.boxing: to box something is to pack it inside, so LAIC holds CON

blocks.note: laic = lay, not professional, so amateur
a con is a scam

annotation.surface: An amateur boxing match turns out to be fixed, and the outcome is over quickly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boxing' looks like the sport, but it only puts one piece inside another. LAIC, meaning lay rather than clergy, stretches to amateur, as a layman is.
annotation.definitionFit: Laconic speech is brief and uses as few words as possible.

entries.clue: Number first to forage on river with its banks cleared (4)

indicatorNotes.with its banks cleared: a river's banks are its edges, so the outer letters of RIVER go
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, IVE sits on F, following it

blocks.note: first letter of forage
RIVER without its outer R and R

annotation.surface: An animal goes foraging along a river whose banks have been stripped bare.
annotation.walkthrough: A river's banks are its two sides, and a word's sides are its first and last letters, so clearing them leaves IVE.
annotation.definitionFit: Five is a plain example of a number, so the definition is a category the answer belongs to.

entries.clue: Join compiler coming in commando? (7)

indicatorNotes.coming in: I comes into the middle of SOLDER

blocks.note: to solder is to join metal
the compiler is the setter, who refers to themself as I

annotation.surface: An invitation for the crossword setter to sign up with the commandos.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Compiler' is the crossword setter, who writes themself into the clue as I. The question mark flags that a commando is only one kind of soldier.
annotation.definitionFit: A commando is an example of a soldier, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: Husband steers clear of upsets and quarrels (6)

indicatorNotes.steers clear of: H avoids the word, so it is dropped from HARROWS

blocks.note: H = husband, the standard abbreviation
to harrow is to distress or upset; H is then removed

annotation.surface: A husband avoids scenes and domestic rows.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Quarrels' looks like arguments, but a quarrel is also a crossbow bolt, an old word for an arrow.
annotation.definitionFit: A quarrel is a short heavy arrow fired from a crossbow.

entries.clue: Snow on to higher ground penetrating outskirts of Dundee (4)

indicatorNotes.penetrating: UP pushes into the middle of DE
indicatorNotes.outskirts of: a town's outskirts are its edges, so the first and last letters of Dundee

blocks.note: first and last letters of Dundee
heading up, to higher ground

annotation.surface: A weather report: snow falling on the hills around Dundee.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Snow' is the weather in the surface, but as a verb it means to deceive with flattering talk. Dundee is a Scottish city.
annotation.definitionFit: To snow someone is to fool them with a smooth line, which is to dupe them.

entries.clue: Dreadful rain over British Island's capital city (7)

indicatorNotes.Dreadful: RAIN is made dreadful, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram of RAIN
O = over, the cricket abbreviation
B = British
I = island, as on maps

annotation.surface: Awful weather sweeps over the capital of a British island.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface points to London or somewhere rainy in the British Isles, but the city is in Kenya.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is a bare category: Nairobi, Kenya's capital, is one city of that kind.

entries.clue: Disrespect demonstrated by unsilenced mob surprisingly! (4,9)

indicatorNotes.surprisingly: the letters end up in a surprising order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: A noisy crowd shows its contempt, to everyone's surprise.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that dumb insolence is silent, so an unsilenced mob is the very opposite of what it describes.
annotation.definitionFit: Dumb insolence is disrespect shown without words, through looks or manner, a term from military discipline.

entries.clue: Aunt Sally's happy family? (8,5)

blocks.note: an Aunt Sally is a target of ridicule
stock = family line, and a laughing one is happy

annotation.surface: A remark about a relative and her cheerful household.
annotation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is an old British pub game where sticks are thrown at a dummy's head, so the name means someone everyone takes shots at. Stock is ancestry, as in 'of good stock'.
annotation.definitionFit: Both an Aunt Sally and a laughing stock are people set up to be mocked.

entries.clue: Ill-bred university lecturer embraces endless twisted debauchery (7)

indicatorNotes.embraces: UNI L wraps its arms round CIV
indicatorNotes.twisted: VIC is turned round to CIV

blocks.note: uni = university
L = lecturer
VICE without its end is VIC, reversed to CIV, which goes in after UN

annotation.surface: A rude academic caught up in some unending, perverse vice.
annotation.walkthrough: Uni is short for university. 'Debauchery' tempts you towards a longer word, but it is only VICE, trimmed and turned.
annotation.definitionFit: Uncivil means lacking manners, which is how someone badly brought up, ill-bred, behaves.

entries.clue: Copy detailed response by art institute (7)

indicatorNotes.detailed: de-tailed: REPLY has its tail, the last letter, cut off
indicatorNotes.by: by means beside, so ICA stands next to REPL

blocks.note: REPLY without its tail
the ICA is the Institute of Contemporary Arts in London

annotation.surface: A gallery sends a thorough reply to a request for a copy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' reads as thorough, but it means de-tailed: remove the last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A replica is a copy of something, especially an exact reproduction of a work of art, which suits the art institute.

entries.clue: One could have groupies excluded from audition (4)

indicatorNotes.from audition: audition is hearing, so the word comes from what is heard

blocks.note: excluded = banned, and it is the sound of that word that counts

annotation.surface: A pop star's fans turned away from a talent audition.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Audition' looks like a tryout, the scene a band belongs in, but here it just means hearing.
annotation.definitionFit: A band is a group of musicians, the kind of act that attracts groupies.

entries.clue: Gets a load of contest points (5)

blocks.note: to vie is to contest
W and S, west and south, two compass points

annotation.surface: Someone collects a pile of points in a competition.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gets a load of' is slang for takes a look at; it has nothing to do with winning lots of points.
annotation.definitionFit: To get a load of something is to take a look at it, to view it.

entries.clue: Chinese society's brief clothing capturing centre of attention (4)

indicatorNotes.brief: TOGS cut short loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.capturing: to capture is to take prisoner and hold, so TOG holds N inside it

blocks.note: TOGS = clothes, shortened
middle letter of attention

annotation.surface: A Chinese society's skimpy outfits draw all eyes.
annotation.walkthrough: Togs is an informal word for clothes. 'Brief clothing' looks like a skimpy outfit, but it means the word TOGS cut short.
annotation.definitionFit: A tong is a Chinese secret society, especially one in a Chinese community abroad.

entries.clue: Provocative dance's vulgar ending succumbs to a minor adjustment (5)

indicatorNotes.succumbs to: R gives way to A, which takes its place

blocks.note: twerking is a sexually provocative dance
last letter of vulgar, removed from TWERK
the letter A, which takes the place of R

annotation.surface: A racy dance loses its crude finish after a small change to the choreography.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vulgar ending' looks like a description of the dance's finale, but it is just the R at the end of 'vulgar'.
annotation.definitionFit: Tweak began as a sharp pinch or twist and now means any small fine-tuning, a minor adjustment.

entries.clue: Woman say from the South Circular area (5)

indicatorNotes.from the South: in a down clue, read from the bottom up, so EG turns to GE

blocks.note: hen = woman, as in hen party
say = for example, EG; reversed to GE

annotation.surface: A woman from the south of the country, perhaps.
annotation.walkthrough: 'South Circular' is a London ring road, which is why the clue feels like it is about London; the words split as 'the South' and 'Circular area'.
annotation.definitionFit: A henge is a prehistoric circular enclosure, like Stonehenge.

entries.clue: Great job making French bread? (4,4)

blocks.note: an exclamation of praise for a job well done
bread is slang for money, and making it means earning it, here in the French city of Nice

annotation.surface: Praise for a baker who has turned out a fine baguette.
annotation.walkthrough: 'French bread' looks like baguettes, but bread is slang for money, and making it means earning it, here in Nice. The question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Nice work' is what you say to someone who has done a great job.

entries.clue: A sign car vacated garage earlier on (6)

indicatorNotes.vacated: GARAGE is emptied of its insides, leaving G and E
indicatorNotes.earlier on: GE goes earlier, in front of MINI

blocks.note: GARAGE vacated, emptied of its middle letters
the Mini, a classic British car

annotation.surface: Someone moved the car out of the garage earlier and put up a sign.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Car vacated garage' reads as the car driving away, but 'vacated' works on 'garage' alone, emptying it of everything but its ends.
annotation.definitionFit: Gemini is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

entries.clue: Ordinary Democrat going through unimagined nightmare (6)

indicatorNotes.going through: going through means passing into, so D enters REAL

blocks.note: O = ordinary, as in O level
not imagined, so real
D = Democrat; it goes inside REAL after the R

annotation.surface: An ordinary party member suffers a bad dream he never saw coming.
annotation.walkthrough: O level was the old British school exam at 16, Ordinary level, so O stands for ordinary.
annotation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful, drawn-out experience, which is a nightmare in the loose sense.

entries.clue: Lothario initially's avoiding flirting or touching (7)

indicatorNotes.avoiding: L keeps away from the word, so it is taken out of DABBLING

blocks.note: first letter of Lothario
dabbling = flirting with an interest without committing; L is then removed

annotation.surface: A womaniser is, for once, keeping his hands to himself.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flirting' suggests the Lothario's romancing, but it means dabbling, as in flirting with an idea.
annotation.definitionFit: To dab is to press lightly and briefly, as with a cloth on a stain, so dabbing is a light touching.

entries.clue: Getting tense - what for? (8)

blocks.note: T = tense, the grammar abbreviation
to give someone what for is to tell them off; a wigging is a telling-off

annotation.surface: Someone is getting anxious and asking why.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Getting tense' reads as growing nervous, but 'Getting' is the definition, meaning understanding. A wigging is a British word for a scolding.
annotation.definitionFit: Twig is informal British for understand, so twigging is getting it in the sense of 'I get it'.

entries.clue: Fine service, hard and fast (4-3)

blocks.note: 'I'm fine' = 'I'm well'
a dinner service is a set of plates

annotation.surface: A tennis serve that is good, powerful and quick.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Service' and 'fast' suggest tennis, but service is crockery here. Hard and fast means firmly fixed, not quick.
annotation.definitionFit: Something well-set is firmly fixed in place, which is what hard and fast means.

entries.clue: Wage war ultimately with extraterrestrial visitor? (7)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so the final letter of 'war'

blocks.note: a wage is income
last letter of war

annotation.surface: A call to fight the alien invader to the bitter end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wage war' reads as a phrase, but 'Wage' is a noun giving INCOME. The question mark allows an alien to count as one example of an incomer.
annotation.definitionFit: An incomer is someone arriving from elsewhere, and an alien visitor arrives from as far away as it gets.

entries.clue: Meal taken by most of old France constitutes cake (6)

indicatorNotes.taken by: to be taken by is to be taken in, so the meal is taken into GAU

blocks.note: GAUL, the old Roman name for France, without its last letter
tea = an evening or afternoon meal

annotation.surface: A French meal whose centrepiece is a cake.
annotation.walkthrough: Tea in Britain can be a meal as well as a drink, either afternoon tea or the evening meal.
annotation.definitionFit: Gateau is a rich layered cake, from the French word for cake.

entries.clue: Withdraws books probing core elements of Einsteinian physics (4)

indicatorNotes.probing: BB pushes in between E and S

blocks.note: middle letters: E from Einsteinian, S from physics
B = book, doubled for the plural

annotation.surface: A library recalls the books that dig into relativity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Core elements of Einsteinian physics' sounds like relativity theory, but it asks for the centre letter of each word.
annotation.definitionFit: Ebb is the tide going out, and by extension anything that recedes or withdraws.

entries.clue: Valued creature's partially disabled (5)

blocks.note: the letters sit in the middle of disabled, between DI and D

annotation.surface: A prized animal is partly disabled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Partially disabled' reads as a description of the creature, but 'partially' tells you to take part of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: The sable is a weasel-like animal valued for its fine fur.

entries.clue: Improvised performance on your bike! (4)

blocks.note: jazz singing improvised with nonsense syllables
a British exclamation meaning go away

annotation.surface: A street busker is told to push off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On your bike!' is British slang for 'Go away!', and so is 'Scat!'.
annotation.definitionFit: Scat singing is vocal improvisation in jazz, and 'Scat!' is an order to leave.

entries.clue: Sweet Fanny Adams upsetting pack animal engenders sanction (4)

indicatorNotes.upsetting: in a down clue, YAK is turned upside down to KAY

blocks.note: sweet Fanny Adams = nothing at all, so O
the yak is a Himalayan beast of burden, reversed to KAY

annotation.surface: Someone called Fanny Adams upsets a yak and gets punished for it.
annotation.walkthrough: Sweet Fanny Adams, or sweet FA, is British slang for nothing whatsoever. 'Sanction' can mean a penalty, but here it means approval.
annotation.definitionFit: Sanction as a verb means to authorise, and okay as a verb means to give the go-ahead.

entries.clue: Beginnings of friendship in rough male company (4)

indicatorNotes.Beginnings of: take the first letter of each word that follows

blocks.note: first letters of friendship, in, rough, male

annotation.surface: A friendship forms among a gang of tough men.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Male company' reads as a group of men, but 'company' alone is the definition. A firm is also slang for a gang of criminals or football hooligans, which suits the picture.
annotation.definitionFit: Firm is a plain synonym for a business company, from the Italian firma, a signature.

entries.clue: Cold arena leads the French to screw up (7)

indicatorNotes.leads: C and RINK go in front of LE

blocks.note: C = cold, as on taps
a skating rink is an arena
le = the, in French

annotation.surface: An ice rink puts the French team ahead, only for them to blow it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Screw up' reads as fail, but here it means crumple, as you would screw up a piece of paper.
annotation.definitionFit: Screw up here means crumple, as with a sheet of paper, and crinkling makes the same creases.

entries.clue: Crib most ideas going round - oddly that's ground breaking (7)

indicatorNotes.going round: the letters are turned round to read backwards
indicatorNotes.oddly: take the odd-numbered letters: 1st, 3rd, 5th and so on

blocks.note: odd-numbered letters C,I,M,S,I,E,S, then read backwards

annotation.surface: A student copies most of their ideas, and somehow it passes as groundbreaking work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ground breaking' reads as innovative, but split in two it describes an earthquake literally breaking the ground.
annotation.definitionFit: Seismic activity is earthquakes, when the ground literally breaks.

entries.clue: Gym culture so unorthodox it produces dangerous opponent (4,8)

indicatorNotes.unorthodox: the letters are set out in an unorthodox order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: A gym's culture is so strange that it breeds a fearsome rival.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes the gym the source of a tough fighter, which suits the answer nicely.
annotation.definitionFit: An ugly customer is a person who is nasty to deal with, a dangerous opponent.
